name: Ty Segall
label: Drag City
lede: Ty Segall grew up surfing in Laguna Beach and put out three albums in 2012 alone. Since then he's toured in a baby mask, sung from behind the drums in Fuzz, and kept releasing records nearly every year.

eras.title: A surf kid, a reality show and a cassette
eras.text: Segall grew up in Laguna Beach, took up surfing at ten, and went to a high school MTV filmed. Music came with Mikal Cronin and a string of bands, then a move to San Francisco, where John Dwyer of Thee Oh Sees put out his first album.

years.h: Ty Segall is born in Laguna Beach and takes up surfing at ten
years.p: He was adopted; his father is a lawyer and his mother an artist.

years.h: MTV sets up cameras at Segall's high school
years.p: Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County shoots there from 2005 to 2007. Segall's own band will film a parody of it.

years.h: Epsilons answer MTV with a Laguna Beach parody
years.p: Segall's grunge band, with his high school friend [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], films a send-up of the show that had been shooting at their school.
years.xp: Segall cycled through bands in these years: [[The Traditional Fools|59897dd7-28bf-4922-9867-c46b5983d240]], Party Fowl, [[Sic Alps|c6f39f9e-b0fc-4614-94a9-ecf648bd8f33]] and Evil Robots among them. Cronin was also in Party Fowl and [[Moonhearts|e35c28f4-ead4-465d-9d99-6bbf8ad7f018]].

years.h: Segall finishes college, then spends eight months building grow boxes
years.p: He has a media studies degree from the University of San Francisco. The boxes are for growing cannabis.

years.h: Horn the Unicorn comes out on cassette
years.p: Segall's first solo tape appears on the small Wizard Mountain label, followed by a split cassette with Superstitions.

years.h: John Dwyer of Thee Oh Sees puts out Segall's first album
years.p: [[John Dwyer|8d941959-2af3-447d-aa39-a215057ae7f5]] befriends him, and Ty Segall arrives on Castle Face, Dwyer's own label.

eras.title: Memphis, Drag City, and a very busy 2012
eras.text: Segall made records faster than most bands book tours: two for Memphis's Goner, a move to Drag City, then a 2012 with a collaboration, a band record and a solo album inside twelve months.

years.h: Memphis garage label Goner picks up Lemons
years.p: Segall's second album comes out on Goner Records.

years.h: Reverse Shark Attack pairs Segall with Mikal Cronin
years.p: The joint album arrives on cassette from Burger Records and on vinyl from Kill Shaman.

years.h: Melted closes the Goner chapter
years.p: Segall's third album, and the last before he signs to Drag City.

years.h: Goodbye Bread lands on Drag City, and critics hear him slow down
years.p: The songs took six months in producer Eric Bauer's basement, then were recorded at Fantasy Studios in San Francisco. Segall calls it the most serious album he has made.
years.xp:
Sessions ran from June 2010 to January 2011. AllMusic's Mark Deming wrote that it "sounds more like a 'real album' than anything Ty Segall has done to date."

Pitchfork put it at No. 31 on its 2011 list. Metacritic scored it 80, and it peaked at No. 44 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

years.h: Charles Moothart wonders how hard a hard rock song could be
years.p: [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] writes one and shows it to Segall. [[Fuzz|1625819f-79d7-4787-b2fb-0e0c260bac85]] is born, with Segall singing from behind the drum kit.
years.xp:
Moothart's own version, as the Fuzz page prints it: he was sitting at home "wondering how hard it would be to write a hard rock song."

Roland Cosio played bass on the first record. Chad Ubovich took over once the band started touring.

years.cap: Ty Segall at The Space Gallery, Portland, Maine, May 2012
years.h: Segall and Tim Presley of White Fence make Hair
years.p: The first Segall album with [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]], on Drag City. They reunite for Joy in 2018.

years.cap: Ty Segall at the Treasure Island Music Festival, San Francisco, October 2012
yt: Live at Pitchfork Music Festival, July 2012
years.h: Segall plugs in a full band for Slaughterhouse
years.p: Out on In the Red, with [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]] on bass, [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] on guitar and Emily Rose Epstein on drums.

years.h: Segall has a third album out before 2012 ends
years.p: Segall's pitch for Twins, the solo record that follows Hair and Slaughterhouse.
years.xp:
He told an interviewer he wanted something like "a total glam Stooges-meets-Hawkwind or Sabbath": "a really heavy record: evil, evil space rock."

The three 2012 albums came out on two labels under three billings: Ty Segall and White Fence, the Ty Segall Band, and Ty Segall alone.

eras.title: Quiet for a year, then fourteen months on one record
eras.text: His father died and he became estranged from his mother. He answered with the acoustic Sleeper, then spent more than a year on Manipulator, his first album on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Segall goes acoustic on Sleeper after his father's death
years.p: Recorded January to March 2013 in San Francisco, after the death of his father, Brian. The song Crazy addresses his estrangement from his mother.
years.xp:
Segall said he was not in a good spot, with his father gone and relationship trouble on top. He recorded on an eight-track at home, then at a friend's house, and thought the songs were demos until they turned into the album.

On the record, he said, "It was necessary for me to put that out there." Pitchfork's Evan Minsker called it his most focused album.

For the tour he put together the Sleeper Band: Sean Paul on guitar, Andrew Luttrell on bass, [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] on drums.

years.cap: Ty Segall drumming and singing with Fuzz, Rock en Seine, Paris, August 2015
years.h: Fuzz debut with Segall on drums and Moothart on guitar
years.p: Roland Cosio plays bass on the October album; Chad Ubovich takes over later.
years.xp: The second album, II, came out in October 2015. Ubovich said it was the first time the band wrote together: "We all kind of did something we've never done before."

years.h: Manipulator takes 14 months and peaks at No. 45
years.p: Co-produced with [[Chris Woodhouse|cb9a3eab-d598-4977-ae54-1e85d4529b1a]], who also recorded and mixed it. It is Segall's first album on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Fourteen months was far longer than any earlier Segall record took. Metacritic scored it 81 and Pitchfork gave it 7.8. The Guardian called it "an unadulterated joy from start to finish."

It also reached No. 8 on the US alternative albums chart and No. 73 in the UK.

years.h: Wand join Segall's GOD? label and then his tour
years.p: Through GOD?, his imprint at Drag City, Segall signs the Los Angeles band Wand and takes them on the road.

eras.title: Sloppo, then the Freedom Band
eras.text: Segall moved to Los Angeles and made his strangest record, then two cut live in the room. Steve Albini recorded the band that became the Freedom Band, and the albums got longer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Emotional Mugger · Wikipedia: Ty Segall
yt: Ty Segall & The Muggers live on KEXP, January 2016
years.h: Segall pulls on a baby mask and becomes Sloppo
years.p: On the road with the Muggers for Emotional Mugger, he wears the mask and goes by Sloppo. The album was announced with a VHS tape.
years.xp:
The Muggers were [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], [[Emmett Kelly|81169a01-84eb-46e2-83af-f6bda1e0da5c]], Kyle Thomas, [[Cory Hanson|cf2f8c4f-00ae-41c9-91b7-294b2747c11a]] of Wand and Evan Burrows. The VHS went to Pitchfork in November 2015, and a website explained "emotional mugging."

Reviews split. Metacritic scored it 79. The Guardian called it "a bad trip rather than a mellow high," while AllMusic heard "a stiff shot of raw, cocky joy." It reached No. 136 on the Billboard 200.

years.big: "He just wants to help you make what you want to make."
q: He just wants to help you make what you want to make.
years.h: A second Ty Segall, cut live with Steve Albini
years.p: Segall on [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], who recorded the band playing together in one room. Warm Hands (Freedom Return) runs over ten minutes; Orange Color Queen is about Denée.
years.xp:
Segall on Albini: "There's no ego." The players, [[Emmett Kelly|81169a01-84eb-46e2-83af-f6bda1e0da5c]], [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] and Ben Boye, became known as the Freedom Band.

Ten tracks in 36 minutes. Metacritic scored it 82, and Pitchfork gave it 8.0.

years.h: Segall writes the theme for Jordan Klepper's Comedy Central show
years.p: He composes the music for The Opposition with Jordan Klepper, and in 2018 for the series Corporate.

years.cap: Ty Segall at Ebrovision festival, Spain, August 2017
years.h: Freedom's Goblin opens with a song for his dog
years.p: Nineteen tracks and 74:48 from four studios, most engineered by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. Fanny Dog leads off, and Hot Chocolate's Every 1's a Winner gets covered.
years.xp:
Segall on the concept: "The theme is the anti-theme, and the idea is to be free." [[Fred Armisen|b1bad7e7-18fd-4c1d-9a64-66c3696209ac]] plays percussion, and Denée Segall sings lead on one track and took photos. It closes with the 12-minute And, Goodnight.

Metacritic scored it 84 and Pitchfork gave it 8.1. It peaked at No. 117 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: He keeps changing the rules and keeps releasing
eras.text: Into his thirties Segall kept testing rules: an album with no guitars, a synth record made in his own studio, an acoustic one at home, an instrumental one. He added side bands too, from GØGGS to Wasted Shirt with Brian Chippendale.

years.h: Ty Segall makes a whole album without a guitar
years.p: A guitarist first, he sets the instrument aside for all of First Taste.

years.h: Wasted Shirt puts Segall next to Brian Chippendale
years.p: Segall and [[Lightning Bolt|978a36f7-85c6-44ca-a02e-7564e8fa8284]] drummer [[Brian Chippendale|2de5109e-2713-46dd-8de5-f64ee000da49]] release Fungus II as [[Wasted Shirt|bcba7375-6862-4636-888b-00c486c8b959]].

years.h: Fuzz come back with III
years.p: Segall is still behind the drums. The single Returning comes out in July, the album on October 23.

years.cap: Ty Segall and the Freedom Band at Shaky Knees, October 2021
yt: Ty Segall & Freedom Band live on KEXP, February 2022
years.h: Harmonizer takes its name from Segall's Los Angeles studio
years.p: Co-produced by [[Cooper Crain|889452cf-b293-480d-9b1d-1959490530c7]], with his wife Denée Segall featured.

years.h: Segall stays home for Hello, Hi
years.p: Mostly acoustic and mostly quiet, recorded at home in his own studio.

years.h: Critics welcome a long, knotty Three Bells
years.p: Segall's fifteenth album, on Drag City.

years.h: Segall sings a lullaby for Yo Gabba Gabbaland!
years.p: Animals Are Sleeping goes out on the children's show's revival.

years.h: Months after Three Bells, an album with no vocals
years.p: Love Rudiments is entirely instrumental.

years.h: Possession arrives, and NPR's Tiny Desk follows
years.p: His seventeenth album comes out May 30. The Tiny Desk concert is published August 22.

years.h: Chrome lands in August, after a January EP of BBC sessions
years.p: Segall's newest album is out August 28.
